name: linked-zero-width-topk-grad
rationale: The zero TopK parameters set srcWidth and K to zero. Every unconditionally selected top-4 helper exits on its initial four-elements-greater-than-srcWidth check before prefix linkage, while K zero prevents postfix destination writes, leaving the bounded device-array output unchanged.

name: concatenate-two-half4-tensors-along-x-through-one-merged-pointer
rationale:
A two-input tensor concatenation along x. A thread whose x is below the first tensor's width addresses src0 and one above it addresses src1, and the two addresses meet in a `phi ptr addrspace(1)` whose arms root in DIFFERENT descriptor bindings. That merge is the whole point: Logical SPIR-V has no pointer value that can be either buffer, so `native/psb_value_select.rs` rewrites it into the value domain -- load both candidates and select the loaded values. Measured with covgain.sh against every cased corpus source plus every public fixture, this 158-line module reaches 8 coverage rows nothing cased reaches, all in that file, including `apply_value_domain_rewrite`, `rewrite_cross_binding_pointer_merges_to_values::vreplay` and `rewrite_scalar_ptr_byte_loads`.

The dispatch is 8x3x3 against bounds of 6, 2 and 2, so 48 of the 72 threads take one of the three early returns and 24 do the copy. Of those, 16 read src0 (x < 4) and 8 read src1, so a merge that collapses to either arm is caught at 8 or 16 of the 24 destination slots: src0 carries values 1..115 and 400.. and src1 carries 200.. and 300.., which share no lane.

Every stride is a distinct parameter member -- src0's row stride is the split width itself, src1's is a separate member, and the two slice strides and the destination's row and slice strides are three more -- and all five differ (4, 2, 8, 4, 8, 16), so reading the wrong member of the 17-integer parameter block moves the read or the write. The destination x offset is 1, which puts the written block off the buffer origin: slots 0, 7, 8, 15, 16, 23, 24 and 31 are never written and must keep their fill, and every one of the 128 destination halves starts at a distinct value above 1000 that no source can produce.

The relu flag is on, so each loaded half4 passes through `air.fmax.v4f16` against zero. Lane 1 of every source element is the negation of lane 0, so the relu is observable at every one of the 24 writes -- lane 1 must read +0 and lanes 0, 2 and 3 must survive unchanged. A dropped relu leaves a negative half in lane 1 at all 24.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: vertex-id-generated-position
rationale: Six vertex invocations use the low two ushort vertex-id bits to generate two triangles spanning the target; the typed position observer captures the resulting four fragment positions byte-exactly.

name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bin
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element; the exact callback is loop-free and returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. The one-bin histogram parameters force every active scalar lane to bin zero, and the poisoned counter makes the bounded global-atomic write observable byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-five-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 5 and receives exact float4 zero from all four linked _uber_clear bodies. A seven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry writes the selected zero to both required poisoned output textures, with binding zero captured byte-exactly.

name: atan2-on-the-axes
rationale: air.atan2.f16 (6 corpus sources) and air.atan2.f32 (1) had no authored case and they are the last two members of the arctangent family that can get one: air.fast_atan2.f32 cannot, because at float width SPIRV-Cross renders the GLSL Atan2 as precise::atan2 while fast::atan2 and precise::atan2 disagree on a third of ordinary arguments, so a fast_ case would assert a MoltenVK limitation rather than a translation. The way past that is to ask only where IEEE-754 fixes the answer regardless of how the implementation computes it: the axes, the diagonals at infinity, and both signed zeros. Every row answers +-0, +-pi, +-pi/2, +-pi/4 or -3pi/4, so the only thing left to round is the constant itself and a 1-ULP approximation error in the arctangent cannot move any of them. The signed-zero rows carry the claim: atan2(-0, +1) must return -0 and not +0, and atan2(-0, -1) must return -pi and not +pi. The origin is deliberately absent, because fast::atan2(0, 0) is NaN where precise::atan2(0, 0) is 0 and it is the one argument in this family that discriminates between the two Metal variants -- a case asking it would be recording which variant a runtime happened to reach. Every argument is read from a buffer so nothing folds and results are bit-cast into one uint buffer with halves zero-extended.

name: the-exposure-floor-is-what-fmax-returns
rationale:
The cyclic AIR is bounded by one authored input: uniform member 24 (the sample count, at byte 120) is -1, and the loop is entered only when that member is greater than zero, so the accumulation over the 1D luminance texture never executes a single iteration and the running sum enters the tail as the phi's zero initializer.
The observed word is the exposure the kernel stores back into autoexposure member 1, and it is exactly the floor constant air.fmax.f32 is called with. Both inputs to the blend are authored zero: the stored exposure starts at 0 and the sum is 0, so the difference the blend scales is 0 and the blended exposure is 0 whatever the two exponentials return -- the case does not depend on air.exp.f32 or air.fast_exp.f32 being accurate, only on their being finite, because their result is multiplied by an authored zero. So the value reaching fmax is zero (or, if an exponential is a ULP off, a value on the order of 1e-14), and fmax against 1e-5f returns 1e-5f in every case. That is the whole answer: a lowering that returns the other operand, that takes a minimum, or that drops the floor entirely stores zero instead, which is also the authored initial byte pattern, so the qualification's differ-from-initial rule catches it too.

name: clamping-instead-of-wrapping-in-eight-families
rationale:
Eight uncovered air.* families in one invocation: air.add_sat.u.v3i8, air.sub_sat.u.v3i8, air.abs_diff.{u.i32,u.v2i16,u.v4i16,s.v4i32}, air.rhadd.u.i16 and air.mad_sat.s.i32 -- 18 corpus sources between them. All nineteen words were derived by hand before the GPU was asked and all nineteen came back as derived. Every family here is one where the WRAPPING version of the same arithmetic is a plausible lowering, so every lane names the wrapped answer it rejects.

addsat(200, 100) on a uchar is 255, not 44: the sum clamps at the type's maximum instead of wrapping. subsat(10, 100) is 0, not 166. The third lane of each, 255+1 and 255-1, sits one step from the same boundary on the side that does not clamp, so a lowering that clamped unconditionally is caught too.

absdiff is where an unsigned subtraction is most tempting and most wrong. absdiff(5u, 10u) is 5, not 4294967291; at ushort width absdiff(0, 65535) is 65535, not the 1 that 0 - 65535 wraps to. The signed member is the sharpest: absdiff(INT_MAX, INT_MIN) is 4294967295, which does not fit in the signed type at all -- the difference overflows int32 to -1 and abs(-1) is 1, so a lowering that subtracted at the operand width answers 1 here instead. That the result type of a SIGNED absdiff is UNSIGNED is the reason the true answer is representable, and Metal's own front end enforces it: assigning it to an int4 does not compile.

rhadd(3, 4) is 4. The rounded half-add is (a + b + 1) >> 1 while the plain hadd is (a + b) >> 1, and 3 and 4 are the smallest pair that separates them -- hadd answers 3.

madsat(100000, 100000, 0) is 2147483647. The exact product is 10^10, which saturates to INT_MAX; a plain multiply-add wraps to 1410065408.

The twentieth word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

name: linked-zero-destination-grid-sample-input-gradient
rationale: The authored destination extent is zero in every dimension. The sole invocation fails the format-specific entry bounds check before coordinate division, interpolation, source access, destination access, or any linked-function call, leaving the bounded poisoned output unchanged.

name: write-four-bytes-into-a-one-dimensional-storage-texture
rationale: The first authored device evidence for air.write_texture_1d.u.v4i32, and the carrier for the two image shapes whose SPIR-V capability the Dim enumerant does not settle. Dim 1D is enabled by either Sampled1D or Image1D and the type's Sampled operand decides which; the rule read that operand for the storage arm and not for the sampled one, so a write-only texture1d claimed both and demanded a capability for an image the module does not contain. Eight threads each write one texel, every lane derived from the thread index with different arithmetic per lane, so a dropped or shifted coordinate and a permuted lane order are both content mismatches rather than a silently identical image.

name: write-four-bytes-into-a-storage-texel-buffer
rationale: The texture_buffer half of the same fixture, pinning air.write_texture_buffer_1d.u.v4i32 -- a symbol no corpus source contains, so no corpus host could ever have covered it. Dim Buffer is the mirror of Dim 1D: enabled by either SampledBuffer or ImageBuffer, with the Sampled operand choosing. This texture's four lanes use different arithmetic from the 1D texture's, so a write that lands on the wrong destination is a mismatch on both cases at once.
